questions.question: According to Article 243 I of the Constitution, the Governor of a state constitutes the Finance Commission for every ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• According to Article 243 I of the Constitution, the Governor of a state constitutes the Finance Commission for every **5 years**.
 
• The Finance Commission is tasked with reviewing the financial position of the Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
• It makes recommendations on the principles governing the distribution of resources between the state and these local governments.
 
• This periodic review ensures that the financial needs of local bodies are met effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Finance Commission plays a crucial role in maintaining fiscal federalism in India.
 
• It ensures that the financial resources are adequately allocated to various levels of government to meet their expenditure needs.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and are subject to acceptance by the government.

questions.question: What is the value of 1 electron volt (eV), which is especially used for nuclear science?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1 electron volt (eV)** is a unit of energy commonly used in the field of nuclear science and particle physics.
 
• It is defined as the amount of kinetic energy gained or lost by an electron when it is accelerated through an electric potential difference of one volt.
 
• The value of **1 eV** is **1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**.
 
• This unit is particularly useful because the energies involved in nuclear reactions and particle interactions are typically very small, and using electron volts makes these values more manageable.
 
• The electron volt is not only used in nuclear science but also in various other fields such as solid-state physics and quantum mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of the electron volt was introduced to provide a more convenient unit of energy for atomic and subatomic processes.
 
• In terms of practical applications, electron volts are often used to describe the energy of electrons in electron microscopes, the energy levels of electrons in atoms, and the energy of photons in different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• The **joule** (J) is the SI unit of energy, and it is a much larger unit compared to the electron volt.
 
• To convert electron volts to joules, you can use the conversion factor: **1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**.
 
• Conversely, to convert joules to electron volts, you can use the conversion factor: **1 joule = 6.242 × 10¹⁸ eV**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race and caste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 15**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 15** of the Constitution of India specifically prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• This Article ensures that the state shall not discriminate against any citizen on these grounds, promoting equality and fairness.
 
• It is a fundamental right enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, which deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 15 is essential for protecting the rights of individuals and ensuring a just and equitable society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 15(1)** states that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any of them.
 
• **Article 15(2)** further prohibits any restriction on access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment, or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads, and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds or dedicated to the use of the general public.
 
• These provisions are critical in ensuring that all citizens have equal access to public facilities and opportunities.
 
• Article 15 has been a cornerstone in various landmark judgments promoting equality and non-discrimination in India.

questions.question: The process of measuring various physical and chemical properties of the rocks and fluids within a wellbore is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**well logging**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Well logging** is the process of measuring various physical and chemical properties of the rocks and fluids within a wellbore.
 
• This technique involves using various tools and instruments to gather data, which is crucial for understanding the geological formations and the potential for oil and gas production.
 
• Common measurements include resistivity, porosity, density, and acoustic properties, among others.
 
• Well logging helps in making informed decisions about drilling, reservoir management, and enhanced oil recovery techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drilling** is the process of creating boreholes in the earth's surface to extract oil, gas, or other subsurface resources.
 
• **Reservoir modelling** involves creating a simulation of a reservoir to predict its behavior under various conditions.
 
• **Enhanced oil recovery techniques** are methods used to increase the amount of crude oil that can be extracted from an oil field.
 
• Well logging is a critical step before employing any of these techniques to ensure the accuracy and efficiency of the operations.

questions.question: What is the difference between a somatic cell and a reproductive cell?

options.text: Somatic cells undergo mitotic cell division while reproductive cells undergo meiotic cell division.
The somatic cells have mitochondria but the reproductive cells do not have any mitochondria.
Somatic cells do not contain any chromosome while reproductive cells have their own chromosome.
The somatic cell and reproductive cell are neither diploid nor haploid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Somatic cells** undergo mitotic cell division, while **reproductive cells** undergo meiotic cell division.
 
• Somatic cells are **diploid** (having two sets of chromosomes), whereas reproductive cells (gametes) are **haploid** (having one set of chromosomes).
 
• Somatic cells make up most of the body's tissues and organs, while reproductive cells are involved in sexual reproduction.
 
• During mitosis, somatic cells produce identical daughter cells, maintaining the chromosome number, whereas meiosis in reproductive cells results in four non-identical daughter cells with half the chromosome number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Somatic cells include cells of the skin, liver, lungs, etc., while reproductive cells include sperm and egg cells.
 
• Errors in mitosis can lead to conditions such as cancer, whereas errors in meiosis can result in genetic disorders such as Down syndrome.
 
• Both types of cells contain mitochondria, and both types have chromosomes, though their chromosome numbers and types of division differ.

• **Haemoglobin** is a protein in **red blood cells** responsible for oxygen transport.
 
• Immunoglobulins are produced by B cells (a type of white blood cell) in response to specific antigens.
 
• The immune response involves the recognition of foreign antigens and the production of antibodies to target and neutralize them.

• **Organelles** are the membrane-bound structures within eukaryotic cells that compartmentalize various chemical functions.
 
• These structures include the **nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus**, and others, each performing specific roles necessary for the cell's survival and functionality.
 
• By segregating different biochemical processes, organelles enhance the efficiency and regulation of cellular activities.

• Disruption in the function of any organelle can lead to cellular dysfunction and is associated with various diseases.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for producing ATP, the cell's energy currency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mitochondria** is often referred to as the "**powerhouse of the cell**".
 
• It is responsible for producing **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**, which is the main energy currency of the cell.
 
• ATP production occurs through a process called **cellular respiration**, which involves the breakdown of glucose and other nutrients.
 
• The mitochondrion has its own DNA and is believed to have originated from an ancient symbiotic relationship between a primitive eukaryotic cell and a prokaryotic cell.
 
• This organelle is essential for energy-intensive processes within the cell, such as muscle contraction and active transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **structure of the mitochondrion** includes two membranes: an outer membrane and a highly folded inner membrane. The folds of the inner membrane are called **cristae**.
 
• The space inside the inner membrane is known as the **matrix**, which contains enzymes, mitochondrial DNA, and ribosomes.
 
• Mitochondria are also involved in other important cellular processes such as **apoptosis (programmed cell death)**, calcium storage, and the regulation of the cell cycle.
 
• Defects in mitochondrial function can lead to a range of metabolic disorders and are linked to conditions such as **mitochondrial myopathy** and **Leigh syndrome**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the structural and functional unit of an organism?

__
 
• The **cell** is the basic **structural and functional unit** of all living organisms.
 
• Cells are the smallest units of life that can replicate independently, and they are often called the "building blocks of life".
 
• There are two main types of cells: **prokaryotic** cells, which lack a nucleus, and **eukaryotic** cells, which have a nucleus.
 
• Cells carry out essential functions such as energy production, nutrient processing, and waste elimination.

• **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate) is a molecule that carries energy within cells.
 
• The **mitochondria** are organelles within the cell that produce ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• The **nucleus** is an organelle in eukaryotic cells that contains most of the cell's genetic material.
 
• Cells can be specialized to perform specific functions, such as muscle cells, nerve cells, and blood cells.
